title: Shared compactification and finite clopen compact-support summands
statement:
Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(k)$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $O=\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi$, and $A_n=O/(\varpi^n)$ for $n\geq1$ [def-pur-conventions]. Let $g:X\to Y$ be separated of finite type between finite-type $k$-schemes, without assuming $Y$ separated over $k$ [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let $I$ be finite and let $j_i:X_i\hookrightarrow X$ be pairwise disjoint open and closed immersions covering $X$, with $g_i=g\circ j_i$ [def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-closed-immersion]. Empty components and the empty cover of $X=\varnothing$ are allowed.

Use the ordinary small pro-etale derived categories, their bounded constructible subcategories and pullback [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility, def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. At a fixed positive level $n$, let $r_i=Lj_i^*$ and let $E_i$ be zero insertion under the finite-clopen equivalence [lem-pur-finite-clopen-derived-decomposition].

There exists a compactification $c=(a,p)$ of $g$, and every chosen such compactification gives $c_i=(a\circ j_i,p)$ of $g_i$, with the SAME proper part $p:\overline X\to Y$ [def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. The schemes $X,Y,X_i,\overline X$ are Noetherian, the maps $j_i$ and $g_i$ are separated of finite type, and $\dim\overline X\leq d$ for some integer $d\geq0$ (take $d=0$ if $\overline X$ is empty).

The functor $E_i$ is exact and is both a left and a right adjoint of $r_i$. It preserves bounded constructibility, agrees with exact extension by zero $j_{i,!}$ [def-weil-extension-by-zero], and gives $K\cong\bigoplus_iE_ir_iK$. The adjunction identification is normalized to the identity after restriction to $X_i$. There is a natural unit-compatible comparison $a_!E_i\cong(a\circ j_i)_!$ obtained by descending the ordinary open-extension comparison. For $F_g^c=Rp_*a_!$ and $F_{g_i}^{c_i}=Rp_*(a\circ j_i)_!$ [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed], it yields
$$b_{i,n}:F_g^cE_i\xrightarrow{\sim}F_{g_i}^{c_i},\qquad
F_g^cK\xrightarrow{\sim}\bigoplus_iF_{g_i}^{c_i}r_iK.$$
These are natural derived-category isomorphisms; the second is the image of the displayed finite biproduct decomposition. On bounded constructible inputs they agree with the compactification-independent functors through the canonical compactification comparisons. For $I=\varnothing$, $K=0$ and the displayed direct image is the empty direct sum.

proof.text: A field is Noetherian (its only ideals are zero and the unit ideal). Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] to the structure maps of $X$ and $Y$. Thus both are Noetherian, in particular quasi-compact; [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated] makes $Y$ quasi-separated. The hypotheses of [thm-nagata-compactification] are therefore satisfied for $g$, without separatedness of $Y$ over $k$. Choose $c=(a,p)$. The rest of the argument works for any such choice: $a$ is open, $p$ proper, and $pa=g$ by [def-weil-compactifications-refinements].

source.place: Conclusion of Nagata compactification; Noetherian hypotheses from Stacks morphisms.tex Tag 01T6 (lemma-finite-type-noetherian) and properties.tex Tag 01OY (lemma-locally-Noetherian-quasi-separated)

proof.text: Each $X_i$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian]. For an affine open $V\subseteq X$, $j_i^{-1}V$ is a closed subspace of the quasi-compact affine space $V$, hence is quasi-compact (extend any open cover by the complementary open and take a finite subcover). Thus $j_i$ is a quasi-compact open immersion, so is finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-qc-open-immersion-finite-type]. The finite-type composition clause of [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change] makes $g_i$ finite type, and likewise makes $X_i\to X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ finite type, so $X_i$ is a finite-type $k$-scheme as the compactification category requires. To check separatedness directly, $X_i\times_Y X_i$ is the open subscheme of $X\times_Y X$ where both coordinates lie in $X_i$. The inverse image of the closed subscheme $\Delta_g(X)$ there is precisely $\Delta_{g_i}(X_i)$, so [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change] makes $\Delta_{g_i}$ closed. The diagonal of $j_i$ is an isomorphism, hence closed. Finally composing the identifications with open subschemes gives an open immersion $a_i=a j_i$, with $pa_i=g_i$. By [def-weil-compactifications-refinements], $c_i=(a_i,p)$ is a compactification; its proper part is literally $p$.

proof.text: Properness of $p$ includes finite type. Compose $p$ with the finite-type structure map of $Y$, using [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change]. Thus $\overline X$ is finite type over $k$, and [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] makes it Noetherian. Apply [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type] to obtain a finite integer bound for its Krull dimension; enlarge it to a nonnegative integer $d$. For the empty scheme take $d=0$. This proves all the stated finiteness assertions for every chosen compactification, including compactifications with extra boundary components.

proof.text:
At level $n$, use the module and unbounded derived equivalences of [lem-pur-finite-clopen-derived-decomposition]. Zero insertion has the following Hom sets in either category:
$$\operatorname{Hom}(E_iM,H)=\operatorname{Hom}(M,r_iH),\qquad \operatorname{Hom}(H,E_iM)=\operatorname{Hom}(r_iH,M).$$
Indeed all other components of a tuple of morphisms are maps to or from zero, hence unique. Composition is componentwise, proving naturality, both adjunctions and their triangle identities. In module categories insertion is exact because kernels and cokernels are componentwise. The stated derived equivalence is termwise, so derived insertion is the induced exact functor. The inclusions and projections of the component tuples give $K\cong\bigoplus_iE_ir_iK$ (their composites are the Kronecker identities and their finite sum is $1_K$). A tuple with one bounded constructible entry and zero entries elsewhere is bounded constructible by the last part of the cited equivalence. Thus $E_i$ preserves bounded constructibility. The same calculation covers an empty component, whose category is zero. In Lean, the generic categorical transport calculation is isolated as lem-pur-clopen-product-adjoints. The original insertion theorem is assembled from this calculation, the actual intrinsic restriction equivalence and the componentwise constructibility bounds.

proof.text: On module sheaves, [lem-weil-extension-by-zero-adjunction] gives another left adjoint $j_{i,!}$ to $r_i$. By [lem-weil-pbc-conjugate-iso-unit-equation], the identity of $r_i$ determines a unique unit-compatible natural isomorphism $E_i\cong j_{i,!}$. Its restriction to $X_i$ is the identity: the insertion unit is the identity, and on objects of the localized site over $X_i$ the extension presheaf of [def-weil-extension-by-zero] is exactly the given sheaf, so its unit is the identity under this identification. Exactness of $j_{i,!}$ is [lem-weil-extension-by-zero-exact]. By [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated] these exact functors act termwise on derived categories. Their comparison and its inverse descend by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property]; their inverse and unit identities descend as equalities of natural transformations. This identifies the derived insertion from step 4 with exact derived extension by zero with the asserted normalization. The insertion assertion is reduced to the general finite-product adjunction lemma. Exactness proves triangulatedness. Its constructibility clause is obtained by transporting the diagonal unit and off-diagonal zero objects through openSquareDerivedPullbackModel, then applying finite_clopen_constructibility_bounds to the original cohomological bounds and constructible cohomology. Restriction preservation is proved separately from finite_clopen_constructibility_bounds, transported to the actual intrinsic pullback by openSquareDerivedPullbackModel. Intrinsic constructibility is transported across isomorphisms using the restriction comparison to constant-module constructibility.

source.place: Tags 03DI (lemma-extension-by-zero), 03DJ (lemma-extension-by-zero-exact); categorical unit comparison from categories.tex Tag 0B65 and exact derived descent from derived.tex Tag 015F

proof.text: On module sheaves the composite $a_!j_{i,!}$ is left adjoint to $j_i^*a^*=(a j_i)^*$ by [lem-weil-extension-by-zero-adjunction] and [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction]. Here the restriction equality simply evaluates a sheaf on the same scheme over $\overline X$. The other left adjoint is $(a j_i)_!$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-conjugate-iso-unit-equation] with this identity of right adjoints to obtain the unique unit-compatible isomorphism. After step 5 this is $a_!E_i\cong(a j_i)_!$. All open-extension functors are exact by [lem-weil-extension-by-zero-exact]. Their termwise comparison, inverse and unit equation therefore descend through [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] to the unbounded derived categories. Apply the single functor $Rp_*$ to this isomorphism. The formula of [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed] identifies its source and target as $F_g^cE_i$ and $F_{g_i}^{c_i}$, giving $b_{i,n}$. Naturality is preserved by descent and by applying $Rp_*$.

proof.text:
The finite-biproduct comparison for $F_g^c$ is elementary here. On sheaves $a_!$ is additive and preserves finite sums: maps from $a_!(\bigoplus M_i)$ correspond by its adjunction to tuples of maps from $M_i$, so this is the coproduct of the $a_!M_i$. Its termwise derived functor has the same property. For $Rp_*$, the adjunction $Lp^*\dashv Rp_*$ of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations] gives, for each $T$,
$$\operatorname{Hom}(T,Rp_*\prod M_i)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(Lp^*T,\prod M_i)\cong\prod_i\operatorname{Hom}(T,Rp_*M_i).$$
Thus it preserves finite products, hence the corresponding biproducts. Its maps are additive, as also seen directly by termwise direct image on complexes and the derived functor. Apply $Rp_*a_!$ to the inclusions and projections in step 4 and use step 6 on each summand. This gives exactly $F_g^cK\cong\bigoplus_iF_{g_i}^{c_i}r_iK$, naturally in $K$. For $I=\varnothing$, step 4 gives $K=0$; $a_!$ preserves the initial zero object and $Rp_*$ the terminal zero object. The image and the empty sum are both zero.

proof.text: For canonical comparison existence, take a bounded etale origin of each intrinsic bounded constructible object using finiteRing_constructibleDerived_origin. The comparison functor from bounded-below etale complexes to intrinsic complexes is fully faithful. Descend fixedCompactSupportOriginIso by conjugating with origin isomorphisms; full faithfulness proves naturality and independence from the witness, and normalization on every witness gives uniqueness. The etale compactification cocycle cancels the intermediate comparison factors; uniqueness descends identity and composition to clopenSupportCanonicalComparison_coherence. The component-independence assertion clopenSupport_independent remains the original named open step: on etale origins it requires compatibility of the normalized open-extension composition with the canonical compactification comparisons, followed by descent. Once this assertion is supplied, apply it on each constructible restricted object; naturality of the canonical comparison on each projection K to E_i r_i K proves clopenSupportSumMap_compactification by biproduct projections. Its composition with the componentwise comparison cocycle proves clopenSupportIndependentSumComparison_eq, including empty sums.
